## International flights LAX to Nairobi (NBO), late Dec 2026 out and about Jan 10–16, 2027 back

**Bottom line:** Book **Turkish Airlines LAX–IST–NBO round trip as one ticket, using multi-city booking, with the Istanbul stopover on the way home.** It is the only airline in this set that lets you add 2–4 nights in Istanbul on the same fare, and US-origin economy tickets can get **2 free hotel nights**. Budget **about $1,300–$1,800 per person** for festive-season economy, or about $1,400–$1,900 with seats and fees. Public fares from Turkish, KLM and Qatar start around $1,000–$1,150, but those are off-peak "from" prices. Departures Dec 19–23 sit in peak demand, so expect $300–$700 more. **These December figures are my estimates, not quoted fares.** Book by late October or early November 2026.

### Airline comparison (economy, round trip, per person, estimates for the travel dates)
| Airline / hub | Advertised "from" fare | Expected fare for Dec 19–23 out / Jan return | Travel time each way | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Turkish via IST** | from $1,000 (TK.com, off-peak) | **$1,250–$1,750** | LAX–IST about 13h (TK10, daily, overnight); IST–NBO about 6h (overnight, arrives early morning). About 22–26h total. Return IST–LAX about 14–15h | Free stopover hotel and Touristanbul tours. Bags: 2 x 23kg in most US economy fares. Best for adding Istanbul |
| **Qatar via DOH** | from about $1,010 | $1,400–$1,900 | LAX–DOH about 15h35 (QR740, A350-1000) plus DOH–NBO about 5h15. About 22–24h | Strong product. A Doha stopover is possible, but it doesn't help with Istanbul |
| **Emirates via DXB** | LAX–DXB sale fares from $746 (not to NBO) | $1,450–$2,000 | LAX–DXB about 16h50 (EK216, departs 16:40) plus DXB–NBO about 4h45. About 23–26h | Often the most expensive over the holidays |
| **KLM via AMS** (often with Kenya Airways) | from $1,136 | $1,400–$2,100 | LAX–AMS about 10h45 plus AMS–NBO about 8h30. About 21–24h | Good timings. Schiphol in winter can bring weather delays |
| **Ethiopian via ADD** | US "from" fares about $1,446 | $1,300–$1,800 | **No LAX service.** Ethiopian dropped Los Angeles (replaced by Houston). You'd connect LAX to IAD, EWR, ORD or IAH on United, then ADD, then NBO. 26h+ | Only worth it if clearly cheaper. More connections and a longer trip |

A Google Flights search for LAX–NBO usually shows Turkish or Qatar as the cheapest one-stop options. Search NBO and the specific travel dates directly. Kenya Airways and Delta both fly JFK–NBO nonstop, but from LAX that adds a third leg.

### Building the Istanbul stopover (Turkish)
- **How to book:** use Multi-city on turkishairlines.com, or the Stopover option. Example legs: LAX–NBO on about Dec 20 via a short IST connection; NBO–IST on about Jan 11; IST–LAX on about Jan 14 or 15. A stopover on a single TK ticket usually costs little or nothing extra compared with a straight round trip. Compare prices both ways.
- **Free hotel rules (Stopover program):**
  - The IST connection must be **at least 20 hours**.
  - The ticket must be issued by Turkish (number starts with 235) and be a round trip in one booking that begins and ends in the same country.
  - Some cheap fare classes, reported as N and R, are excluded. Check before you buy.
  - Economy gets 1 night in a 4-star hotel, and **departures from the US, Canada or Australia get a bonus night, so 2 nights** in total. Business class gets a 5-star hotel.
  - Apply **at least 72 hours** before the first flight.
  - The hotel can be used on the outbound **or** the return, not both.
  - Nights 3 and 4 are at your own cost, about $100–$200 per room per night for a mid-range hotel in Sultanahmet or Karaköy.
- **Touristanbul:** a free guided city tour with a meal, for international-to-international connections of **6–24 hours** on a TK ticket. Be at the desk 30 minutes early, and be back at least about 1h25 before your next flight. Use it if you choose a long connection instead of a full stopover.
- **Which direction:** **the way home (about Jan 11–14) is better.**
  - The trip out stays short over the holidays, so you reach Kenya sooner.
  - Your safari days aren't eaten into.
  - Istanbul hotels after New Year cost less than over New Year's Eve.
  - You avoid carrying winter clothes on the 15kg bush flights. Leave a city bag at your Nairobi hotel or with your ground operator.
  - Istanbul in January is about 3–10°C and often rainy, so bring layers.
- **Entry requirements:** US citizens can enter Türkiye **without a visa** for up to 90 days in any 180 (the e-visa requirement was dropped in Dec 2023). Kenya requires an **eTA**, about $30–35 for US citizens. Apply at least a week ahead; processing takes about 3 working days.

### Kenya domestic flights (Wilson airport (WIL) or Nanyuki)
| Route | Airlines | One-way fare per person (estimate) | Flight time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nairobi Wilson to Nanyuki (NYK) for Ol Pejeta | Safarilink, Airkenya, FlyALS | **About $150–$210** (round trip about $310–$325). Safarilink fares start at about KES 6,300 for promo seats | 35–45 min | You could also drive, 3–4h, about $150–$250 per vehicle for a transfer |
| Nairobi Wilson to Mara airstrips | Safarilink, Airkenya, Mombasa Air Safari (seasonal) | **About $260–$330** in high season (round trip about $520–$650) | 45–75 min, depending on how many airstrips the plane stops at | Airstrips: Ol Kiombo, Musiara, Mara Serena, Keekorok, Kichwa Tembo, Olare Orok, Angama Mara, plus Mara North and Naboisho strips. Book the strip your camp names |
| **Nanyuki to Mara, direct** (the conservancy-to-conservancy link) | Safarilink, Airkenya | **About $376 (low season) to $409 (high season)** | About 35 min nonstop to Musiara, or about 1h10 with stops | Avoids going back through Nairobi. About 7 or more Safarilink departures a week |
| Mara to Wilson (to return) | Same airlines | About $260–$330 | 45–75 min | Late-morning or midday departures connect to evening international flights from Nairobi |

- **Baggage:** **15kg in total per person, including hand luggage and camera gear, in soft-sided bags only.** Maximum bag size is about 90 x 65 x 35cm. Excess baggage can be bought ahead in 10, 20 or 30kg blocks up to 48 hours before departure, and only flies if there is space. Without it, heavy travellers may have to buy an extra seat.
- **Budget for a Nairobi to Ol Pejeta to Mara to Nairobi loop: about $800–$950 per person** in festive season. The same loop driving to Ol Pejeta and flying the rest is about $600–$700.
- **Booking:** book the bush flights early, because December holiday flights sell out. Your camp or safari operator can often book them, and sometimes at a lower rate.

### Booking tips
1. Book the international flights first, ideally **before about Nov 1, 2026**. Outbound Dec 19–20 is usually cheaper than Dec 22–23. Avoid arriving on Dec 24 or 25 because of transfer and camp logistics.
2. Use **one ticket for all international legs**, so a missed connection is the airline's responsibility. Leave at least 3 hours between landing at NBO and a Wilson departure. Wilson is a separate airport about 30–45 minutes across town.
3. On Turkish, choose EcoFly or a higher fare. Check the fare class before buying to confirm it qualifies for the free stopover hotel, then request the hotel at least 72 hours ahead.
4. Set Google Flights price alerts for LAX–NBO and the multi-city LAX–NBO / NBO–IST / IST–LAX routing.

### Air and transport budget per person
- International round trip with the Istanbul stopover: about $1,300–$1,800
- Domestic flights: about $800–$950
- Kenya eTA: about $35
- 0–2 extra paid Istanbul nights: about $50–$200 per person
- **Total: roughly $2,200–$3,000 per person**, which leaves about $2,500–$3,500 per person for conservancy camps, park fees and Istanbul spending.

**About these figures:** Turkish, KLM and Ethiopian "from" fares, the Safarilink baggage rules and the Nanyuki–Mara fares come from sources. Everything else is an estimate for festive-season dates, because no live December 2026 fares were available. Several fare and operator pages were blocked by the network, so some details come from search-result summaries rather than full pages.

## Ol Pejeta Conservancy (Laikipia): accommodation, fees and activities for late Dec 2026 to early Jan 2027

**Location:** Ol Pejeta is in Laikipia, below Mt Kenya near Nanyuki. It is about 200 km and 3.5–4 hours by road from Nairobi. It is **not** in the Masai Mara, so a Mara conservancy such as Naboisho, Mara North, Ol Kinyei or Olare Motorogi has to be planned as a separate stop. A common pairing is 2–3 nights at Ol Pejeta plus 3–4 nights in a Mara conservancy, with a scheduled light-aircraft flight between them (Nanyuki to the Mara).

### Conservancy fees (non-resident, 2026 OPC tariff)
- **Daily entry fee:** USD 110 per adult, USD 55 per child, USD 32 per student. You pay it for every 24 hours inside the conservancy.
- It includes the **Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary** and self-guided game viewing (including Baraka, the blind black rhino).
- The all-inclusive camps (Porini) already include it. Most other properties charge it separately.
- 2027 rates may rise a little. Expect about $110–120.

### Activities (2026 OPC prices, per person)
| Activity | Price |
|---|---|
| Northern white rhino visit (Najin, at Morani's enclosure) | ~$70 |
| Lion tracking (2 hrs, with the research team) | ~$70 |
| Night game drive (2 hrs, 7–9pm or 9–11pm, book a day ahead) | ~$70 |
| Chimpanzee sanctuary | included in entry |
| Behind-the-scenes chimps, dog tracking, rhino monitoring, guided bush walks | ~$40–100 each (estimate) |

At Porini Rhino, Bush Camp, Kicheche and Safari Cottages, night drives and walks are included.

**Warning about the northern white rhinos:** In May 2026, social posts attributed to caretaker Peter Esegon claimed that Fatu had been shot dead. I found this only on low-quality aggregator sites (mexc.com) and **could not confirm an official Ol Pejeta statement**. Check the conservancy's news page before relying on seeing both Najin and Fatu.

### Accommodation for Dec 20, 2026 to ~Jan 10, 2027
All prices are USD per person per night sharing (pppn) unless noted. The last column adds the entry fee where it is not included.

| Property | Style | Festive rate | Early-Jan rate | Included | Real cost pppn with entry |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Porini Rhino Camp** (about 10 tents, eco tented) | tented, all-inclusive | **$695** (Dec 20–Jan 2) | **$601** (from Jan 3, 2027) | Full board, drinks (beer, house wine, G&T), shared day and night drives, chimp visit, airstrip transfers, **conservancy fees**. Trust levy +$5 (2026) / +$10 (2027) | **~$700 festive / ~$611 Jan** |
| **Ol Pejeta Bush Camp** (Asilia; moves seasonally) | tented, all-inclusive | **$860** (Dec 20–Jan 5) | **$690** (from Jan 6) | Full board, house drinks, day and night drives, airstrip transfers, laundry. Entry fee probably extra (confirm) | ~$970 / ~$800 |
| **Kicheche Laikipia** (6 tents) | upscale tented | **~$1,135** (Dec 15–Jan 10; 4-day package from $4,025) | similar | Full board, drinks, shared drives, night drives, walks, canoe and bike. Conservancy fees extra | ~$1,245 |
| **Ol Pejeta Safari Cottages** (OPC-owned) | private cottages | **$690** (Dec 16–Jan 6) | **$596** (from Jan 7) | Full board, drinks, **private vehicle and guide**, night drives, walks, transfers. Entry fee extra | ~$800 / ~$706 |
| **Sweetwaters Serena Camp, Morani Wing** | large tented hotel | **$670 per double tent = ~$335 pp** (Dec 23–Jan 1), plus $45 pp Christmas Eve surcharge | **$480 per double = ~$240 pp** (from Jan 2) | Full board only. Game drives and fees extra | ~$335 + $110 + ~$80 drives (estimate) = **~$525 festive / ~$430 Jan** |
| Sweetwaters Serena, Standard Wing | tented | ~$195–300 pp full board (estimate; sources vary) | similar | Full board only | ~$400–500 with fees and drives |
| **Pelican House** (OPC self-catering, sleeps up to 8) | house | $100 pp (2–4 people) | same | Self-catering only. Bring food and a vehicle | $210 + vehicle and driver |
| **OPC public / special campsites** | camping | **$70 per adult** | same | Pitch only. Bring your own gear and vehicle | $180 + vehicle, gear, food |

### Getting there
- **By road:** about 3.5–4 hours from Nairobi via Nyeri or Nanyuki. A private transfer or safari vehicle with driver costs about $250–350 one way per vehicle, or $175–250 per day if the vehicle stays with you (estimates). This is the only practical way to camp or self-cater.
- **By air:** Safarilink or Airkenya from Wilson Airport to Nanyuki (NYK), about 40–45 minutes. Fares are about **$134–200 one way, ~$270–400 return** per person, with festive season at the top of that range. The all-inclusive camps provide airstrip transfers. Nanyuki also has direct scheduled flights to the Mara, so flying works well if Ol Pejeta is followed by a Mara conservancy.

### Recommendations
1. **Best value: Porini Rhino Camp, 2–3 nights.** It is the cheapest true conservancy tented camp where the fees, drinks, night drives and chimp visit are all included.
   - 3 nights in the festive period: about **$2,100 pp**. 3 nights from Jan 3: about **$1,830 pp**.
   - Add fly-in ($300–400 pp) or a road transfer (~$150 pp for two travelers).
   - Porini also gives combination discounts with its Mara conservancy camps (Porini Lion in Olare Motorogi, Porini Mara in Naboisho). This makes it a natural pairing with the requested Mara conservancy stay.
   - Schedule Ol Pejeta for **Jan 3 or later** to drop out of festive pricing.
2. **Budget alternative: Sweetwaters Serena Camp (tented), 2 nights, by road with a safari vehicle and driver.**
   - About $430–525 pp per night including entry and drives, versus about $700 at Porini.
   - **Camping** on an OPC campsite ($70 + $110 entry pp per night, plus vehicle, gear and food) only saves money if a budget operator is already supplying the camping kit and driver.

**Rough Ol Pejeta budget for 2 nights per person:** about $900–1,400. That covers lodging, entry, a $70 rhino or lion-tracking add-on, and a share of ground transfer, and uses roughly 15–25% of a $5–6k per-person budget.

All camp rates are rack or agent rates from the search results; agent and operator net rates are often 10–20% lower. The official OPC tariff PDF and the agent rate pages were blocked to direct fetching, so the figures come from search-result extracts of those pages. Treat the Serena standard-wing rates, the Bush Camp and Kicheche fee treatment, and the transfer costs as estimates.

## Masai Mara private conservancy camps: mid-range options for Dec 2026 / Jan 2027

**Caveats.** Every camp and rate-aggregator site (porini.com, kenyasafari.com, chaloafrica.com, africanmeccasafaris.com, go2africa.com) was blocked by the network proxy. Fetching pages and downloading with curl both failed. All numbers below come from search-result snippets of those pages, so treat them as close estimates and confirm with the camp or agent before booking. All prices are USD per person per night (pppn), two people sharing a tent.

**Geography.** Ol Pejeta Conservancy is in Laikipia (central Kenya), not the Mara. It is a separate stop, about 4 hours' drive or a short flight from Nairobi. Porini Rhino Camp is the mid-range camp there. In the Mara, the private conservancies are Olare Motorogi, Naboisho, Ol Kinyei, Mara North, Enonkishu and Olderkesi. Note that Porini Mara Camp is in **Ol Kinyei**, not Naboisho, though its guests can also drive in Naboisho.

### Why a conservancy rather than the National Reserve
- **Activities the reserve doesn't allow:**
  - off-road driving to reach sightings
  - night drives with spotlights, for leopard, hyena, aardvark, genet and other night animals
  - walking safaris with Maasai guides
  - bush meals
- **Fewer vehicles:** about 1 vehicle per 700 acres, with usually no more than 5 at a sighting.
- **Fees:** the conservancy fee is roughly $80–150 pppn and is normally built into camp rates. Porini lists $130 for Olare Motorogi and Ol Kinyei, $150 on its free-night offer, and $80–120 at Enonkishu.
- **Reserve fee is extra.** Masai Mara National Reserve entry costs non-residents **$200 per day from July to December and $100 per day from January to June**, on a 12-hour ticket. It is charged only if you go into the reserve, so a conservancy-only stay avoids it. A January reserve day costs half as much as a December one.

### Rates for 20 Dec 2026 – 2 Jan 2027 (festive) and January 2027

| Camp (conservancy) | Festive 20 Dec–2 Jan pppn | From 3 Jan 2027 pppn | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Porini Lion Camp** (Olare Motorogi; top big-cat area, home of the Enesikiria/Moniko lion prides) | $930–1,013 (the $936 "game package" includes conservancy fees) | ~$650–700 (estimate; the Jan–Mar 2026 rate was $650) | All-inclusive. Two-night fly-in package: $1,770–2,745 by season (~$1,920 typical), including return flights from Wilson airport. |
| **Porini Mara Camp** (Ol Kinyei, 18,700 acres, 6 tents) | ~$862 (one snippet; another shows $1,503, which probably includes flights or park fees, so unconfirmed) | ~$600–650 (estimate; Jan–May 2026 was $570; one snippet shows $898 for Jan 2027, likely a package) | All-inclusive; Ol Kinyei and Naboisho conservancy fees included. |
| **Porini Cheetah Camp** (Ol Kinyei) | $927–941 | ~$573–650 (estimate) | All-inclusive. |
| **Kicheche Valley** (Naboisho) | $1,095 | $860 for 3 Jan–28 Feb 2027 | Strong photography focus. |
| **Saruni / Basecamp Eagle View** (Naboisho) | ~$990 | from ~$599–780 | Africanmecca's 15 Dec–10 Jan guide: $2,200 per person for 2 nights plus $780 per extra night. |
| **Encounter Mara** (Asilia, Naboisho) | $940 (20 Dec–5 Jan) | ~$710 | Asilia's simplest camp. |
| **Dorobo Mobile Camp** (Naboisho) | **$620** (20 Dec–2 Jan) | ~$500 (the 1–19 Dec 2026 rate) | **Cheapest true conservancy tented camp found.** A mobile, camping-style camp. |
| **Ol Seki Hemingways** (Naboisho) | n/a | from $810 | |
| **Karen Blixen Camp** (Mara North) | $2,295 per person for 2 nights (15 Dec–10 Jan), +$795 per extra night | from $825 | Flight and conservancy fees may be extra. |
| **Mara Bush Houses** (Basecamp, Mara North) | ~$2,227 per person for 2 nights incl. flights (that is the 2025/26 festive rate, based on 4 people sharing) | n/a | Exclusive-use houses; best for groups of 4 or more. |
| **Topi House** (Ol Kinyei) | **Closed** | | |
| **Naboisho Camp** (Asilia) | $2,250 | $1,240 | Too expensive for this budget. |
| **Mara Nyika / Kicheche Bush** | $3,000+ (snippets look like luxury multi-night or package figures) | | Not mid-range. |
| **Enonkishu / Mara Training Centre** | No published 2026 rates | | Community-run and simpler; conservancy fee $80–120. Ask directly. |
| **Budget road-safari camping into Ol Kinyei / Enonkishu** | ~$250–450 pppn including vehicle | | Operator-dependent estimates. |

**Festive supplements**
- Porini adds a Christmas/New Year supplement on **24, 25, 26 and 31 Dec and 1 Jan**. Sources conflict: one says **$40 pppn**, another says **$100 pppn**. Budget $100.
- Porini also adds a Wildlife Habitat Trust levy of $5 pppn in 2026 and $10 in 2027.

**What Porini includes:** all meals; house drinks (beer, wine, gin and tonic, sodas); shared day and night game drives in open 4x4 vehicles; walks with Maasai warriors; sundowners; airstrip transfers; and daily conservancy fees. Reserve entry and Nairobi–Mara flights are extra, except in the fly-in packages.

**Flights:** Nairobi Wilson to the Mara on Safarilink or Airkenya costs about **$300–450 per person return** for scheduled flights. Porini's flight-inclusive packages work out to about $500–600 return.

### Porini offers and combo packages
1. **4 nights for the price of 3** at all Porini camps. You pay only the conservancy fee (~$150) for the 4th night. Valid on 2026 travel except July–September. It is not yet confirmed for Jan 2027, so ask.
2. **15% off the whole Porini package**, covering camps, conservancy and park fees, and internal flights, for stays of **8 nights or more at Porini camps between 20 Dec 2026 and 2 Jan 2027.**
3. **Laikipia & Mara Safari, 6 days / 5 nights, from $3,580 per person.** It combines Nairobi Tented Camp, Porini Rhino Camp at **Ol Pejeta** (2 nights) and Porini Lion Camp, and includes flights and conservancy fees. This directly fits the wish to see both Ol Pejeta and a Mara conservancy. Festive dates will cost more.
4. **6-night reduced-rate offer** (Porini PDF, July 2026), plus the longer itineraries "Porini Wilderness Experience 7D/6N", "Big Five Porini 5D/4N" and "Signature 12D/11N".

### Wildlife in late December / early January
- **The migration has gone.** The main wildebeest herds left the Mara by November. In late December and January they are on the short-grass plains of the southern Serengeti and Ndutu in Tanzania, where calving runs from about late January to February.
- **Resident wildlife is still excellent, especially in the conservancies:**
  - large lion prides; Olare Motorogi has some of the highest lion densities in Africa
  - cheetah (Naboisho and Ol Kinyei are known for cheetah mothers with cubs)
  - leopard and hyena
  - elephant, giraffe, topi and eland
  - the resident Loita wildebeest and zebra herds
  - newborn gazelles and topi, which draw plenty of predator action
- **Conditions:**
  - The short rains are ending, so the plains are green, there is little dust and the light is good for photography.
  - Expect occasional afternoon showers.
  - Birding is excellent because Palearctic migrant birds are present.
- **Visitors:** there are fewer vehicles than in July–October. The festive weeks are busy and expensive, though, so **book now; small camps of 6–9 tents sell out.**

### Recommendations: 2 best-value options
**Shared budget logic.** Getting under $5–6k per person including LAX–Nairobi flights (roughly $1,400–2,000) means **putting the Mara nights after 2–3 Jan 2027.** Rates fall about 30–35% then, and the festive supplements end.
- Use the festive week for Istanbul, travel days or Nairobi.
- Ol Pejeta is a Porini Rhino Camp stop; check its rate separately. Use it on either side of the Mara stay.

1. **Porini Lion Camp, Olare Motorogi.** This is the best wildlife-for-money pick: a top big-cat conservancy, fully inclusive, with night drives and walks.
   - About 4 nights from 3 Jan using the 4-for-3 offer: 3 × ~$680 + $150 ≈ **$2,200 per person (about $550 a night)**.
   - Add about $400–550 for flights. **Total ≈ $2,600–2,750 per person.**
   - The same 4 nights during the festive period would cost about $3,000–4,000 per person.
2. **Porini Mara Camp or Porini Cheetah Camp (Ol Kinyei), or Dorobo Mobile Camp (Naboisho) for the camping feel.**
   - Ol Kinyei in January with the 4-for-3 offer: about $1,900–2,100 per person for 4 nights, plus flights.
   - Dorobo: about $500 pppn in January and **$620 pppn even during the festive period**. It is the cheapest genuine conservancy tented or mobile camp found, and the best choice if you must be in the Mara over Christmas.
   - Dorobo inclusions and transfers need confirming.
   - Ol Kinyei is also reachable by road (about 5–6 hours from Nairobi), which saves the flight cost.

**Alternative:** Porini's **Laikipia & Mara 6D/5N combo (from $3,580 per person)** covers Ol Pejeta and Olare Motorogi in one booking with flights. In January it is likely about $3,600–4,000 per person, which leaves about $1,500–2,000 for international flights and Istanbul. Doable at the top of the budget.

**Avoid** Kicheche Bush, Mara Nyika, Naboisho Camp and Karen Blixen at festive rates. They break the budget.

## Kenya practicalities for US travelers, Dec 2026 to Jan 2027

Exchange rate assumed: about **1 USD = 129–132 KES** (mid-2026 rate is about 129; the Oct 2026 forecast is about 132).

### Entry and documents
- **Kenya eTA:** US passport holders must have one. It costs **$30** per person (expedited service adds about $100). Apply only on the official site, etas.gov.ke. Standard processing takes about 3 business days, and you should apply at least 72 hours before departure. It allows stays of up to 90 days.
- **Passport:** it needs 6 months of validity and 2 blank pages (standard rule).
- **Istanbul stopover:** US citizens need no visa for Türkiye for tourist stays of up to 90 days. If Istanbul is included, the Kenya entry is a flight from IST. Türkiye is not a yellow-fever-risk country, so it does not trigger a Kenya yellow fever certificate check.

### Health (CDC)
- **Yellow fever:** CDC recommends the vaccine for travelers aged 9 months and older, except for itineraries limited to Nairobi city, Mombasa/coast and North-Eastern. Mara, Laikipia/Ol Pejeta, Amboseli and Samburu are all in recommended zones. A certificate is only *required* when arriving from a risk country. Budget **$200–$350 per person** in the US. Supply is limited (Stamaril), so book a travel clinic now.
- **Malaria:** present in all areas below 2,500 m, including Nairobi and the game parks. Chemoprophylaxis is recommended: atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone; generic about **$50–$150** for about 25 days), doxycycline (about $15–$30), mefloquine or tafenoquine.
- **Other vaccines and health notes:**
  - Routine vaccines, Hep A, Typhoid and Tdap are recommended. A travel clinic consult costs about $100–$200.
  - The current CDC notice covers **dengue** on the coast, which matters for the Diani/Watamu add-on. Bring DEET or picaridin.

### Insurance and medical evacuation
- **AMREF Flying Doctors Maisha Tourist cover** (per trip):
  - Bronze **$10** covers Kenya only.
  - Silver **$24** adds Tanzania and Zanzibar.
  - Gold $32 and Platinum $80 cover more countries.
  - It includes unlimited air evacuation to Nairobi and ground ambulance. Many conservancy camps already include it in the rate; check before buying.
- **Comprehensive travel insurance:** choose a policy with **at least $250k medical evacuation** cover. A week-long comprehensive plan costs $43–$291 (Squaremouth; World Nomads Explorer is about $158 per week). For about 3.5 weeks with trip cancellation on about $5k, expect **$200–$450 per person**. A medical and evacuation-only plan is about $80–$150.

### Nairobi hotels (per room per night, B&B unless noted)
| Hotel | 2026/27 rate |
|---|---|
| Tribe Hotel (Gigiri) | about $218–$469, average about $357 |
| Ole Sereni (overlooks Nairobi NP) | Superior $240–$310, Deluxe $270–$350 |
| Karen Blixen Coffee Garden Cottages | Classic $240–$357 |
| Macushla House (Langata/Karen) | from about $127–$128 per person sharing (about $255 per room) |
| House of Waine (Karen) | from $370 per person; too expensive |
| Hemingways Nairobi | Deluxe suites $645–$1,060; too expensive |
| Giraffe Manor | far too expensive |

**Recommendation:** Ole Sereni, Macushla or Karen Blixen Cottages at **about $250–$350 per room, or $125–$175 per person per night**. A good-value fallback is a Karen guesthouse or a Westlands business hotel at about $120–$180 per room.

### Nairobi activities
- **Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage:** **$20 per person**. Public visit is daily 11:00–12:00 and **closed Christmas Day**. Book online only, with dates released about 90 days ahead (book in late Sept or early Oct for late December). Some sources say Nairobi NP fees may also apply; check when booking.
- **Giraffe Centre:** **KES 1,500 (about $12) per adult**, open 9–5 daily including holidays, paid by card or M-Pesa.
- **Nairobi National Park:** the KWS non-resident fee was **$43**, with a hike to **$80** per adult per day. The hike has been repeatedly suspended by the High Court (Oct 2025, and again in Aug 2026). Budget **$80 to be safe**. Payment is by card or M-Pesa only at kwspay.ecitizen.go.ke. A half-day game drive with vehicle and guide adds about $80–$150 per vehicle.
- **Premium parks:** Amboseli and Nakuru were set at **$90 per adult**, but that is also suspended. Older rates were about $60. Budget $60–$90.

### Getting around and baggage
- **Airport transfers from JKIA:** Uber or Bolt to Westlands is KES 1,200–2,000 ($10–$15) and to Karen is KES 1,800–2,800 ($14–$22), plus Expressway toll. A pre-booked sedan is about $25–$40, and a hotel or camp meet-and-greet is about $40–$60 per car.
- **Bush flights (Safarilink and similar):** **15 kg per person including hand luggage, in soft bags**, maximum 90×65×35 cm. Coast routes (Diani/Ukunda, Vipingo) allow 20 kg. Excess baggage can be pre-bought in 10 kg blocks, and there is **free left-luggage at Wilson Airport**.
- **Nairobi to Diani (Ukunda) flights:** Jambojet is about KES 13,900–14,900 ($105–$115) one way. Safarilink is about KES 14,300–19,250 ($110–$150). Expedia shows fares from $121.

### Tipping (per traveler unless noted)
- **Private driver-guide:** $40–$50 per vehicle per day. On a shared or group safari, $10–$20 per person per day.
- **Tracker or spotter:** $5–$10 per person per day.
- **Camp or lodge general staff box:** $5–$15 per person per night. At small conservancy camps it is $12–$18.
- **Practical budget:** about **$20–$30 per person per day on safari** and about $5–$10 per day elsewhere. Carry crisp post-2013 small USD bills.

### Connectivity and money
- **eSIM:** Airalo uses the Safaricom network, with plans from about $8 per 5 GB up to about $32–$49 for 5–10 GB depending on the plan. No registration needed.
- **Safaricom tourist SIM at JKIA:** about KES 1,000 for 5 GB, 2,000 for 15 GB or 3,000 for 25 GB (30 days). It needs your passport for registration and gives you M-Pesa. Budget **$10–$25 per person**.
- **Money:** the currency is the KES. Cards work in Nairobi and at lodges. Park gates are cashless (card or M-Pesa). USD cash is widely accepted for tips; bring post-2013 notes.

### Safety (US State Dept)
- **Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution** (issued 28 Jul 2026), citing crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and road safety.
- **Level 4 (Do Not Travel)** applies to the Somalia-border counties and to coastal Lamu, Tana River and areas north of Malindi. **Watamu sits just south of Malindi; check the exact boundary.** Diani is not in a Level 4 area.
- Avoid Eastleigh and Kibera, avoid walking at night in Nairobi, and use Uber or hotel cars.

### Weather in late Dec / Jan (short dry season)
- **Nairobi:** about 18–24°C (64–75°F), about 40 mm of rain in January.
- **Mara:** about 27–28°C (81–82°F) by day and cool mornings (10–13°C). Rainfall is about 111 mm in December and 82 mm in January, with occasional storms early in the season. Laikipia/Ol Pejeta is similar and slightly drier.
- **Coast:** hot and humid, 30–32°C.
- **Packing:** soft duffel of 15 kg or less; layers and a fleece for dawn drives; neutral colors (no camo); binoculars; sun hat; headlamp; Type G (UK 3-pin) plug adapter. **Plastic bags are banned in Kenya.**

### Optional add-ons before mid-January (mid-range, per person sharing)
- **Amboseli conservancies:**
  - Porini Amboseli (Selenkay Conservancy) packages include game drives and conservancy fees. Expect about **$450–$650 per person per night** in high season, plus a **$40 per person per night festive supplement on Dec 24, 25, 26, 31 and Jan 1**.
  - Kibo Safari Camp (just outside the park) is about **$380 per double per night** full board (Jan–Feb 2026 rate), so about $190 per person. Add park fees ($60–$90 per day) and a vehicle.
  - Tawi Lodge (conservancy) is from $466–$570 per person and too expensive.
- **Samburu:** mid-range river camps (Samburu Sopa, Ashnil) are about **$250–$550 per person per night**. Elephant Bedroom is about $800 per person; Sasaab is about $2,000 per person.
- **Coast for New Year:**
  - **Diani:** half-board is about KES 14,200–21,000 (**$110–$165**) per person per night at AfroChic. Leopard Beach and Southern Palms are about £894 per person for 7 nights in normal season; **expect +30–60% over Christmas and New Year**. Flights are $105–$150 each way.
  - **Watamu:** Hemingways Watamu is from **$245 per person per night**. Medina Palms is about $300–$550 or more per villa.
  - **Budget:** about **$700–$1,100 per person for 3–4 coast nights**, including flights.

### Per-person practicalities budget (excluding main safari and international air)
| Item | Per person |
|---|---|
| eTA | $30 |
| Vaccines, malaria pills, clinic | $350–$650 (some may be covered by US insurance) |
| Travel insurance | $200–$450 |
| AMREF Maisha (if the camp doesn't include it) | $10–$24 |
| SIM/eSIM | $10–$25 |
| Nairobi hotel, 2 nights | $250–$350 |
| Sheldrick + Giraffe Centre | about $32 |
| Airport transfers | $20–$50 |
| Tips (about 10 safari days) | $200–$300 |

Practicalities alone come to about **$1,100–$1,900 per person**.

Two cautions:
- Most numbers are aggregator or operator quotes. Festive-season rates for Dec 20 to Jan 5 can run 20–60% higher, so treat all lodging figures as estimates.
- The KWS fee status is still in court, so re-check it at booking.

summary:
## Istanbul 3-night stopover: findings (for travel in late Dec 2026 or mid-Jan 2027)

**Exchange rate assumption:** about 48 TRY per USD (USD/TRY was 48.4 in Sep 2026; the lira keeps weakening, so prices quoted in lira tend to rise during the year). I used about $1.15 per €1. All USD numbers are **per person** for 2 people sharing a room.

### Entry and visa
- **US citizens need no visa and no e-visa.** Since Jan 2024 they can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The passport must be valid 6+ months past the stay and have blank pages. Cost: $0.

### Turkish Airlines programs (the best fit is LAX–IST–NBO on Turkish Airlines, which flies both legs)
- **Stopover in Istanbul (free hotel):** needs a layover of 20 hours to 7 days on an international-to-international connection through IST. The ticket number must start with 235, it must be a round trip on one booking that starts and ends in the same country, and N and R fare classes are excluded. Request the hotel at least 72 hours before the flight. The **US is on the extended list**: economy gets **2 free nights in a 4-star hotel** and business gets **3 nights in a 5-star**. Other countries get 1 night economy and 2 nights business. For a 3-night stay you would pay for 1 extra night in economy. The free hotels are assigned, often outside the old city, so confirm the location. Check the exact fare class when booking.
- **Touristanbul (free guided tour):** for layovers of 6 to 24 hours. Any Turkish Airlines ticket with a 235 number qualifies, and the tour includes a meal. Tours leave from and return to IST (one example slot is 08:00–11:30). Register at the desk on the arrivals floor at least 30 minutes before the tour. It is only useful as a day-of-arrival bonus, not for a 3-night stop.

### Mid-range hotels for winter (Jan is low season; Dec 25–Jan 1 costs more)
- Areas: **Sultanahmet** (walk to the main sights) or **Karaköy / Galata** (better food and nightlife, on the tram line). Boutique and mid-range rooms run **€50–90 per night** in low season. Better 4-star boutiques run **about $90–180 per room per night**, with New Year's Eve at a premium.
- Names to check: 10 Karaköy, Galata Rasso Boutique, Pera Bosphorus (Galata), Hotel Niles, Sura Hagia Sophia (Sultanahmet).

### Sights and 2026 entry fees (per person, foreign visitors)
- **Hagia Sophia** upper gallery: **€25 (about $29)**. The Museum Pass does **not** cover it, and the ground-floor prayer area is free.
- **Topkapı Palace** combined ticket (grounds, Harem and Hagia Irene): **about 2,750 TRY / €55 (about $57)**. Some sources give the parts separately at €40 + €20 Harem + €10 Hagia Irene, so budget up to about $80.
- **Basilica Cistern:** **about 1,300 TRY ($27)** in the daytime, more at night. Not on the Museum Pass.
- **Dolmabahçe Palace** combined ticket: **2,000 TRY / about €40 ($42)**. Buy at millisaraylar.gov.tr. Not on the Museum Pass.
- **Galata Tower:** **€30 ($35)**. Open 08:30–18:15, with night entry 19:00–23:00.
- **Bosphorus by public ferry (Şehir Hatları):** short tour **340 TRY ($7)**, long full-day tour to Anadolu Kavağı **640 TRY ($13)**. Turyol and Dentur run 1.5-hour cruises for 250–300 TRY ($5–6).
- **Grand Bazaar and Blue Mosque:** free.
- **Hammam:** Çemberlitaş runs **1,200–3,800 TRY ($25–80)**. Cağaloğlu runs **2,000–4,500 TRY ($42–95)**.
- **Museum Pass Istanbul:** **about 6,500 TRY (about $135–185)**, valid 5 days. It covers Topkapı + Harem, the Archaeological Museums, Chora, the Hagia Sophia History & Experience Museum and the Mosaic Museum. It does not cover Hagia Sophia, the Cistern or Dolmabahçe. **It is not worth it for a 3-night first visit** unless you will see 4 or more of the sites it covers. Buy single tickets instead.

### Getting from the airport to the city (IST is about 45–60 minutes from the center)
- **Havaist bus:** about 265–355 TRY ($6–8) to Aksaray, then the T1 tram for about 42 TRY to Sultanahmet. Some sources quote about €8 total.
- **Taxi:** 1,300–2,400 TRY per car ($27–50), so **$14–25 per person each way**. A pre-booked private transfer costs about $35–55 per car.
- Local transport: an Istanbulkart transit card loaded with about $10–15 per person covers 3 days.

### Food
- Mid-range eating is **1,200–1,800 TRY per day ($25–40)**. A meze-and-main dinner is 700–1,200 TRY ($15–25). Budget **$40–70 per day per person** to allow for a nicer dinner and drinks.

### January weather
- Highs about **9°C / 49°F**, lows about **3°C / 37°F**. About 82 mm of rain over **about 12 rainy days**, with occasional snow and high humidity that makes it feel colder. Bring a warm waterproof layer. Crowds are much smaller than in summer, which is good for indoor sights. Avoid arriving on New Year's Eve unless you want the crowds and premium prices.

### Recommendation
Book LAX–IST–NBO round trip on Turkish Airlines with the **Istanbul stop on the return** (for example Jan 12–15, 2027, flying home to LAX on Jan 15–16). Mid-January is low season and cheaper than the festive peak. Claim the 2 free economy nights and pay for 1 night yourself, or skip the free hotel and book a boutique in Sultanahmet or Karaköy. Plan for 3 days:
- **Day 1:** Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Basilica Cistern, hammam.
- **Day 2:** Topkapı and Harem, Grand Bazaar, Spice Bazaar, short Bosphorus ferry.
- **Day 3:** Dolmabahçe, Galata Tower, dinner in Karaköy.

**Estimated total added cost: about $450–1,000 per person.** About $650 is a realistic midpoint.

All prices are 2026 estimates from the sources listed and should be reconfirmed close to travel because of lira inflation. I could not open the official turkishairlines.com stopover page (blocked here), so the stopover terms come from third-party summaries.
